criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (coral reef monitoring via fluid lensing), rationale (GBR bleaching), single-spacecraft justification, and users/operator/funding all addressed with literature citations. Detail is good though user discussion is brief.

evidence.quote: Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All major requirements addressed: launch site/vehicle with justification, SSO with full COEs, manoeuvres (none until EOL), ground station, access frequency via STK report, 5-year duration and drag-sail EOL. STK screenshots included but no software files shown; some errors (e.g. 'low resolution images which is also desirable') and the inclination plot lacks shown hand calculation.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions summarise each segment and acknowledge risk (Vega E availability), but remain largely a restatement of the design rather than deeper insights or quantitative outcomes.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure with headings, TOC and executive summary; figures have captions but lack figure numbers. References are bare URLs, inconsistently formatted, and Wikipedia is used as a source, which the task disallows. Some garbled sentences (e.g. drag sail paragraph) hurt readability.

Figures captioned but not numbered (e.g. 'STK 3D view of orbit')
Bibliography - Wikipedia cited as [6]; bare URLs, inconsistent formatting

technical_issues.issue: Statement 'A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable' is incorrect/contradictory.
Drag sail paragraph is garbled and contradicts itself ('without thrusters... choose an uncontrolled descent... However, the ZYZZsat is without thrust capability').
Wikipedia used as a source, disallowed by task; references are bare URLs without titles/authors/dates.
Inclination-altitude plot presented without showing the underlying J2 hand calculation.

overall: A well-structured, mostly complete mission design for GBR reef monitoring with sound STK evidence and justified choices. Weakened by internal contradictions in the EOL section, unnumbered figures, missing software files, and improper referencing including Wikipedia.

feedback.summary: A well-structured, mostly complete mission design for GBR reef monitoring with sound STK evidence and justified launch/orbit choices. To reach the top band, resolve internal contradictions (EOL drag-sail, orbit resolution statement), show your J2 hand calculation, include STK software files, number your figures, and replace Wikipedia/bare URLs with properly formatted, credible references.
next_steps: Fix the contradictory statements in the EOL drag-sail paragraph and the orbit section's 'low resolution images which is also desirable' claim, then re-read each section for internal consistency.
Include your STK scenario/software files (appendix or submission package) and show the J2 hand calculation behind your inclination-altitude plot.
Number all figures (Figure 1, 2, ...) and cross-reference them in text; replace Wikipedia and bare URLs with peer-reviewed or primary sources formatted consistently (e.g. IEEE style).

criteria.C1: Accomplished (8/10). Your Introduction clearly covers the primary mission (GBR coral reef monitoring via fluid lensing), the rationale, the single-spacecraft justification, and users/operator/funding, with literature citations. To reach the very top, expand the user discussion (e.g. how CSIRO/BOM would actually use the data) with more specific detail and referencing.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (7/10). All major requirements are addressed: Vega E from Guiana Space Centre with justification, a 600 km SSO with full orbital elements, no manoeuvres until EOL, ground station coverage and access frequency via STK, and a 5-year mission with drag-sail EOL. To improve: include your STK software files, show the J2 hand calculation behind the inclination-altitude plot, and correct the contradictory 'low resolution images which is also desirable' statement.
criteria.C3: Adequate (6/10). Your Conclusion summarises each segment and honestly flags the Vega E availability risk, but it largely restates the design. The next level requires deeper, evidence-driven insights: quantitative outcomes (e.g. revisit time, coverage statistics, data volume) and what they imply for mission feasibility.
criteria.C4: Adequate (5/10). Your structure is clear (headings, TOC, executive summary) and figures are captioned, but they lack figure numbers, and the bibliography uses bare URLs and Wikipedia (disallowed), inconsistently formatted. The garbled drag-sail paragraph also hurts readability. Fix referencing, number figures, and proofread carefully to reach the Accomplished level.
